name: MOROCCO
lead: Morocco sits in the top-left corner of Africa, where the Sahara nearly touches the Mediterranean Sea. Souks (busy markets) sell silks dyed with spices. Walled cities glow rose-pink. Snow covers mountains behind Atlantic surf beaches.
geo: Morocco has three mountain chains: the Rif, the Middle Atlas, and the High Atlas. Berber villages (home of an old people) cling to cliffs above cedar forests.
In the south, the land drops into the Sahara. The dunes at Erg Chebbi rise 150 m and turn gold at sunrise. The Atlantic coast stretches 1,800 km.
animals: The Barbary macaque, Morocco's only wild monkey, scrambles through cedar forests near Azrou. Loggerhead sea turtles nest on southern beaches each summer.
The High Atlas shelters the rare Barbary leopard. The fennec fox has ears like satellite dishes and hunts beetles in the sand at night.
culture: Souks are mazes of craftspeople. Coppersmiths hammer lanterns, weavers knot rugs, and workers dye leather in rainbow vats. Cooks pour mint tea from a great height to make it frothy.
Gnawa musicians play iron clappers and a three-string guembri (a bass lute). Tagine is meat slow-cooked with apricots, olives, and cumin in a cone-shaped clay pot.
history: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fes opened in 859 CE. Berber (Amazigh) peoples have lived in Morocco for 5,000 years. Arab traders came in the 7th century.
In 1777, Morocco became the first country to recognise the United States. France and Spain colonised (took over) it in 1912. King Mohammed V led it to independence in 1956.
wows: Al-Qarawiyyin in Fes is the world's oldest continuously working university.
Morocco holds about 70% of the world's known phosphate, a rock used for plant food.
Erg Chebbi's dunes are 150 m tall, higher than a 40-storey building.
Morocco has nine UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Fes, Marrakech, and Meknes.
Argan oil comes from trees that grow almost only in Morocco.
The Strait of Gibraltar is just 14 km wide, Morocco's nearest point to Europe.
Storytellers and acrobats perform nightly at Marrakech's Djemaa el-Fna square.

myths.fact: In Morocco, goats climb argan trees to eat the fruit. They balance on branches high above the ground.

myths.myth: Moroccan food is always very hot
myths.fact: Most dishes are mild and sweet-smelling. Hot harissa sauce comes on the side, so each person picks how much.
